sourceFacts.fact: Increased oxygenation after normal breathing begins suppresses EPO production and erythropoiesis.
Reduced production and shorter neonatal red-cell lifespan contribute to the physiological Hb nadir.
EPO stimulation later resumes and haemoglobin gradually rises.

validation.pixelReviewNotes: Pixel-to-specification review confirms oxygen up leads through negative feedback to EPO down, then slower production and a qualitative Hb trough. EPO is a radio signal, production a mechanical conveyor, and lifespan an hourglass; no organs or marrow. Ribbon has no axes or values and conveys timing qualitatively. Short neonatal red-cell lifespan is explicitly an additional contributor.
